official_measurement_examples.name: Protected status
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England guidance states all bat species and their breeding and resting places are protected by law.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning standing advice
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England's bat standing advice is a material planning consideration for local planning authorities when bats may be affected.

official_measurement_examples.name: Mitigation licence trigger
official_measurement_examples.fact: A13 guidance requires a mitigation licence where proposed work would otherwise unlawfully affect bats or their breeding or resting places.

official_measurement_examples.name: Low-impact licence scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: CL21 is limited to specified common or widespread bat species, low-conservation-status roosts and registered consultants within the licence conditions.

official_measurement_examples.name: Survey licence distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: CL17 permits defined observation-only survey activity for scientific, research or educational purposes, including informing development projects.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2026 reference evidence
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England published separate bat survey class-licence reference and experience guidance on 3 June 2026 for CL17 to CL20 applications.

official_measurement_examples.name: Licensing tests
official_measurement_examples.fact: Protected-species mitigation licensing may require evidence on purpose, satisfactory alternatives and conservation outcome; a reasoned statement is application evidence rather than planning permission.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Bat survey or mitigation licensing does not itself grant planning permission, establish bat absence or determine parcel development capacity.

core_rules: bat protection law is not proof bats are present on a parcel
bat survey result is not planning permission
planning permission is not a bat mitigation licence
A13 mitigation licence is distinct from CL21 low-impact licence
CL17 survey licence is not a mitigation licence
registered bat consultant status is not a site approval
planning standing advice is not a planning decision
reasoned statement is licence-application evidence not a planning grant
historic bat survey must retain its survey date and season
absence of recorded roost is not proof of bat absence without adequate evidence
bat roost protection does not determine land ownership
licence conditions must be tied to the actual species and roost scope
protected-species licensing does not reserve development capacity
bat compliance does not create access rights
no parcel bat clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
